summary: Alert tagging: many-to-many Tag/Alert, add/remove tag endpoints, tag filter on GET /api/alerts, tags in AlertResponse

acceptance_criteria.text: A Tag entity exists with a many-to-many relationship to Alert via a new join table, added by a new EF migration (and reflected in database/02_AlertServiceDb_Migrations.sql).
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags with one or more tags adds them to the alert and returns the updated alert including its tags.
Tags are de-duplicated case-insensitively (within the request and against tags already on the alert); a tag already on the alert is not added twice.
An alert can have at most 10 tags; a request that would make the alert exceed 10 tags is rejected and nothing is added.
Each tag must be 1-30 characters; an empty/whitespace-only or longer-than-30 tag is rejected with 400.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} removes the tag from the alert.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} returns 404 when the alert does not exist.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} returns 404 when the alert exists but the tag is not assigned to it.
GET /api/alerts accepts an optional 'tag' query parameter and returns only alerts that have that tag.
The 'tag' filter composes (AND) with the existing isActive, severity, createdFrom/createdTo and search filters, and TotalCount/paging reflect the combined filter.
AlertResponse includes the alert's tags (on list, get-by-id, create, update, deactivate and tag operations).

exact_source_files: AlertService.Data.SQL/Configurations/TagConfiguration.cs (new; also configures the Alert<->Tag join table, AlertConfiguration unchanged)
adjacent_dependencies: AlertService.API/Middleware/ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs (maps every unhandled exception to 500; tag-limit overflow must not rely on it)
README.md (API contract section; update only if /implement-story documents the new endpoints)
constraints: Input validation at the API boundary: tag 1-30 chars, trimmed, non-whitespace; max 10 tags per alert; 'tag' query param length-bounded (security: validate all input; no raw SQL, EF parameterized queries only).
Layering: controller -> IAlertService (DTOs only) -> IAlertRepository (Alert/Tag entities); service layer must not reference EF Core.

Tag matching, de-duplication and filtering are case-insensitive; implement provider-agnostically (tests use InMemory/SQLite, prod uses SQL Server), e.g. ToLower() comparison as in the existing 'search' filter.
Database: new schema change only via an EF migration (no manual edits of generated migration/snapshot); join table cascades on alert delete; unique index on Tag name.

Changing IAlertRepository.GetAllAsync's signature breaks existing positional Moq setups in AlertManagementServiceTests (expression trees cannot use optional args); /unit-testing must update those tests. /implement-story therefore builds only the API project (which compiles Data/Data.SQL), not the solution.
Tag-limit overflow needs a defined 400 outcome from the service layer; no existing mechanism exists (middleware only emits 500).
coverage_goals: Behavior coverage of AC1-AC11, including 404 paths, limit boundary (10 ok / 11 rejected), 1/30 vs 0/31 char boundaries, and case-insensitive dedupe/filter.
unresolved_questions: POST /tags success response: assumed 200 OK with the updated AlertResponse (not 201). Confirm.
POST body shape: assumed { "tags": ["a", "b"] } (AddTagsRequest with 1-10 items). Confirm.
POST to a non-existent alert: assumed 404 (not stated in the story).
Tag already on the alert or duplicate in request: assumed silently ignored (idempotent), counted once toward the 10 limit. Confirm.
Tags are trimmed; stored with first-seen casing; matching/uniqueness is case-insensitive. Confirm.
DELETE success response: assumed 204 No Content. Confirm.
Orphaned Tag rows (no alerts left) are kept, not deleted. Confirm.
